**Norfolk Southern Corp (CIK 702165) — freight volume and revenue-intensity trend, FY2022–FY2024**

**Headline:** Volumes were essentially flat-to-slightly-up over the last two years, while revenue intensity (revenue per unit of work) declined in both 2024 and 2023. So the recent pattern is "more/steady volume, less revenue per unit" — i.e., revenue growth did not come from pricing intensity.

**Freight volumes (from the five-year operating statistics table and MD&A volume tables)**

| Metric | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 | 2021 | 2020 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue ton-miles (billions) | 178 | 176 | 179 | 178 | 164 |
| Intermodal units (thousands) | 4,107.7 | 3,822.4 | 3,913.1 | n/a | n/a |
| Coal tonnage (thousands of tons) | 76,702 | 75,892 | 76,664 | n/a | n/a |

- Revenue ton-miles: +1.1% in 2024 (178 vs 176) after −1.7% in 2023 (176 vs 179). Over two years, 2024 is roughly flat versus 2022 (178 vs 179).
- Intermodal units: +7% in 2024 (domestic +5%, international +11%) after −2% in 2023 (domestic −8%, international +8%).
- Coal tonnage: +1% in 2024 after −1% in 2023; utility coal fell 3% in 2024 and 15% in 2023, offset by export coal +7% in 2024 and +20% in 2023.
- Merchandise: 2.3 million carloads in 2024 (62% of railway operating revenues); intermodal 25%; coal 13%.

**Revenue intensity (revenue per thousand revenue ton-miles)**

| | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 | 2021 | 2020 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue per thousand RTM | $68.09 | $69.05 | $71.35 | $62.56 | $59.67 |

- 2024: −1.4% (68.09 vs 69.05); 2023: −3.2% (69.05 vs 71.35). The 2022 peak of $71.35 was driven by fuel surcharge revenue and pricing gains; the subsequent declines reflect lower fuel surcharge revenue, reduced storage service charges, adverse mix and (in 2024) lower intermodal pricing.
- Total railway operating revenues: $12,123M in 2024 vs $12,156M in 2023 (−0.3%), per `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` (FY2024 10-K, accession filed 2025-02-10; FY2023 10-K filed 2024-02-05). So revenue was flat while ton-miles rose ~1%, consistent with the falling per-unit intensity.
- Productivity: revenue ton-miles per railroad employee rose to 8,846 in 2024 from 8,719 in 2023 (after falling to 8,719 from 9,513 in 2022).

**Interpretation and limitations**
- The trend is a volume recovery (mainly intermodal and export coal) paired with weaker revenue per unit of traffic, so revenue intensity has been the drag rather than volume.
- Revenue ton-miles are a company-defined operating statistic, not an XBRL fact; the volume and intensity figures above come from the narrative/statistical tables in the FY2024 10-K (report_end 2024-12-31, chunk IDs 702165/nsc-20241231:38400, :132800, :134400, :40000) and the FY2023 10-K (chunk 702165/nsc-20231231:36800). The structured `financial_facts` table contains revenue but no ton-mile/carload tags, so volumes could not be cross-checked against XBRL.
- The 2024 10-K's five-year table covers 2020–2024; 2021 and 2020 intermodal/coal detail was not retrieved, so those cells are marked n/a rather than estimated.
- MD&A explanations (fuel surcharge, mix, truck competition, natural gas prices) are management's stated drivers, not independently verified causal claims.
